research_scope: Source-free independent Wave2 contextual prerequisite audit of three mathematically justified primitive identities; preserves context-specific structure in full formulations and existing alias ledgers; no source content, external research, certification or gate changes.

aliases.reason: The original second discrete-time martingale variant states its process (X_n,F_n) is integrable, which means E|X_n|<∞ for each n≥0. The first discrete-time and continuous-time martingale formulations explicitly state E|X_t|<∞ at each index, without requiring a common bound, and the conditional-expectation source also uses integrability as finite absolute expectation. The sole shared prerequisite is coordinatewise L¹ integrability for a real random variable at each time parameter; specializing its index set T from nonnegative reals to nonnegative integers gives precisely the discrete-time condition. The process index set, adaptation, filtration, conditional expectation identities, and absence of a uniform L¹ bound remain specified in their respective full source formulations.

The full complete-local-ring formulation uses the canonical unital ring homomorphism R→lim_n R/m^n and requires this map to be an isomorphism. Its missing candidate explicitly requires a unital ring homomorphism having a unital ring-homomorphism inverse, not a mere bijection of underlying sets. This is exactly the generic categorical isomorphism prerequisite when the ambient category is unital commutative rings; in this category inverse arrows are ring homomorphisms. The m-adic inverse limit, topology/completion and local-ring hypotheses remain separate constraints in the parent definition, rather than being ascribed to an arbitrary categorical isomorphism.

The profinite-group parent defines its comparison as an isomorphism of topological groups G→lim_i G_i. Its candidate requires a group homomorphism which is a homeomorphism, equivalently a morphism admitting a two-sided inverse in the category TopGrp of topological groups and continuous group homomorphisms. This is the categorical-isomorphism prerequisite instantiated in TopGrp. Neither abstract group bijectivity nor plain topological homeomorphism is sufficient; group and topology compatibility remain explicitly carried by the full profinite-group parent and the context-specific source occurrence. The inverse-limit-of-finite-discrete-groups condition is not absorbed into generic isomorphism.
